analysis.investment_thesis: Aegis Vopak is an infrastructure play on India's LPG/chemical storage demand with solid 48% operating margins, but at P/E 109 and P/S 31 it's priced for perfection with a PEG well north of 2. The growth story is real but modest (revenue 562→621 Cr, only ~10% YoY), and ROE of 8.7% doesn't justify paying 4.66x book.
key_strengths: Strong tollbooth-style economics: 48% operating margin, 99% gross margin on terminal storage fees
Indian LPG/chemical import tailwinds; Vopak JV parentage provides global terminal expertise
OCF turned sharply positive (478 Cr in FY25) and FCF flipped to +350 Cr after heavy capex
key_risks: Valuation absurd for the growth: P/E 109 vs revenue growth only ~10.5% (2024→2025) = PEG ~10
ROE 8.73% / ROCE 7.01% — below cost of capital; finance cost 193 Cr eats nearly 60% of operating income
Heavily capex-intensive and debt-funded (2,004 Cr borrowings); returns depend on terminal utilization ramp
red_flags: PEG ratio >5 — classic 'hot IPO' overvaluation pattern
Net profit of 127 Cr on 22,244 Cr market cap implies 175x earnings — buying terminals at theme-park prices
analysis.detailed_analysis: What's the story? India imports ~60% of its LPG and a growing volume of chemicals, and Aegis Vopak owns the tanks at the ports. That's a good business — 48% operating margins and 99% gross margins tell you it's a tollbooth. But Peter Lynch's cardinal rule is growth at a *reasonable* price, and there's nothing reasonable here. You're paying 109x trailing earnings and 31x sales for a company growing revenue 10.5% year-over-year with ROE under 9%. The PEG is effectively off the charts. This is a recent IPO riding thematic enthusiasm — exactly the setup Lynch warned about.\n\nThe fundamentals underneath the valuation are mediocre, not exceptional. Finance costs of 193 Cr consume 42% of operating income, ROCE of 7% is below the cost of debt, and the company just raised equity (reserves jumped from 996 Cr to 3,634 Cr) to deleverage — which dilutes the growth story further. I'd want to revisit this at half the current price (P/E ~50) once utilization on new terminals proves out and earnings double. Until then, the story is "good business, terrible stock." Avoid.
